segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Node's `os` module — operating-system information. See [TDD-00024](../tdd/TDD-00024.md)/[ADR-00090](../adr/ADR-00090.md).

notes: `getenv("HOME")`; throws a catchable Error if unset (matches real Node)
caveats: Throws when `$HOME` is unset (`os.homedir()` errors) instead of Node's passwd-database fallback (`getpwuid`), which returns the home dir without throwing.
Consults only `$TMPDIR` (not `$TMP`/`$TEMP`) and keeps a trailing slash — `TMPDIR=/foo/` yields `'/foo/'`, where Node returns `'/foo'`.

notes: Real per-core `{model, speed, times: {user,nice,sys,idle,irq}}` — Linux via `/proc/cpuinfo`/`/proc/stat` parsing, Darwin via `sysctlbyname`/Mach `host_processor_info` — both verified (Darwin on Apple Silicon M4 Pro: `model` = `"Apple M4 Pro"`, live tick counters)

Darwin `speed`: `hw.cpufrequency` is unavailable on Apple Silicon (M-series removed the fixed-clock model), so a fixed `2400` MHz nominal is reported there — byte-for-byte what real Node/libuv reports on the same hardware; an Intel Mac's real value flows through unchanged ([ADR-00569](../adr/ADR-00569.md))
Darwin `times.irq` is always `0` — Mach's per-core tick array has no `irq` bucket (only user/system/idle/nice); real Node reports `irq: 0` on Darwin too, so this is parity, not a gap
Linux `speed` reflects the CPU's current/scaled frequency (from `/proc/cpuinfo`'s `cpu MHz`), not a rated base/max clock — matches what libuv/real Node reports on Linux
Verified on Linux and on Apple Silicon M4 Pro — `totalmem()` matches `sysctl hw.memsize`; Darwin `freemem()` (Mach `host_statistics`) returns a live free-page figure
Always `"\n"` — this compiler is POSIX-only (no Windows target), so there's no real `"\r\n"` case
